name: Safe zones for external fixator pins in the proximal forearm
aliases: proximal ulna Schanz screw safe zone
corridor: Lateral to posterolateral Schanz screw corridor in the proximal or middle third of the subcutaneous ulna, with the forearm neutral, checking that the screw does not tether the radius

positioning.text: Position with the forearm in neutral rotation and the subcutaneous ulna accessible under imaging.

surface_landmarks.text: Palpate the easily recognizable subcutaneous border of the proximal and middle ulna.

incision.text: Make a small incision to bone at each planned Schanz screw site.

superficial_interval.text: Insert Schanz screws into the lateral or posterolateral part of the proximal or middle third of the ulna with the forearm neutral.

deep_interval.text: After insertion, check pronation and supination to make sure the Schanz screw does not tether or contact the radius.

layers.text: Skin, subcutaneous tissue, and the ulnar cortex.

structures_at_risk.text: The posterior interosseous nerve near the proximal radius and the forearm rotation (if the screw contacts the radius) are the concerns; the subcutaneous ulna itself is a safe corridor.

danger_zones.text: Screws that stray toward the radius or the proximal supinator region risk tethering rotation or endangering the posterior interosseous nerve.

retraction_hazards.text: Keep the screw within the ulna and confirm free forearm rotation after insertion.

exposure.text: Provides a safe ulnar corridor for external fixator Schanz screws rather than a formal exposure.

limitations.text: The safe corridor is limited to the lateral and posterolateral proximal-to-middle ulna to avoid the radius and proximal nerves.

indications.text: Indicated for external fixator Schanz screw placement in the proximal forearm.

closure.text: Close each incision loosely around the screw.

complications.text: Complications include restricted forearm rotation if the screw contacts the radius and pin-tract problems.

procedure_applications.condition: A spanning external fixator is applied across the elbow or proximal forearm

questions.question: Into which part of the ulna are proximal forearm Schanz screws placed?
questions.answer: The lateral or posterolateral proximal or middle third of the ulna.

questions.question: What must be checked after screw insertion?
questions.answer: Pronation and supination, to ensure the screw does not affect the radius.

questions.question: In what rotation is the forearm held for insertion?
